content:
Hello, is it possible to create own librarys? I wrote some infrastructure wich every task build. On my own machine one time built modules didn't build again if not changed. How I can do like that with aristotle?

Thanks in Advance.

Do you have a concrete example? Is that library in the same folder? I think (though I was never sure about this) when you do aristotle submit --project-dir . "Prove blabla in file xyz" then it will also upload part of your .lake folder, so that probably will include the compiled version of your own lib too? But @Pietro Monticone or someone else actually working at Harmonic will know better I guess.

Hi @antaris, yes you can use your own library by including its sources in the lake project you submit with aristotle submit --project-dir ..

The CLI includes custom dependency sources from .lake, but excludes compiled files such as .olean. So building locally first does not transfer your build cache.

Hope it's helpful.

The actual project is huge but went to a milestone. The build with aristotle isn't persistent. It needs to build the huge part in every task. Aristotle ran out of budget much faster. Thats the reason I asked if the huge part could be used as "prebuild library" which don't need to build in every task or something like that. Sorry for my english but if I use translator then get banned for using LLM. Actually I use not CLI. I use the web frontend.
